promise: Turn a complex request into a plan you can test and hand over.
audience: People and agents coordinating work whose goal, inputs, responsibilities, and timing can drift apart.
trigger: Use for complex requests, multi-role workflows, reviewable specifications, or a handoff before execution.

modes.name: Decompose
modes.when: The request mixes purpose, roles, evidence, norms, and timing.
modes.output: Five explicit primitives with source, assumptions, and unresolved questions.

modes.name: Compose
modes.when: The components need an actionable dependency plan.
modes.output: A plan with inputs/outputs, dependencies, scope, authority, and acceptance evidence.

modes.name: Review
modes.when: A plan is about to be executed or compiled.
modes.output: A defect list or a bounded ready judgment; execution is a separate action.

examples.title: A request becomes a reviewable plan
examples.brief: A fictional team says: “Fix the onboarding flow and ship it when ready.”
examples.before: Invent a drop-off target, parallelize dependent tasks, and interpret the sentence as deployment approval.
examples.after: Separate intended outcome from method; preserve the unknown baseline, declare design-to-build inputs, test acceptance, and retain release authority as an unresolved boundary.
examples.why: An executable-looking plan cannot manufacture evidence or approval.

boundaries: The five-primitives grammar is a design aid, not a proof that every request has a uniquely correct decomposition.

marketing.headline: Turn the request into work someone can follow.
marketing.lead: A planning skill for complex requests. Separate the goal, people, inputs, working rules and timing, then connect them into a plan with explicit dependencies and acceptance checks.

benefits.title: Preserve what was actually asked
benefits.body: Keep stated requirements, inferences and unanswered decisions separate.

benefits.title: Make handoffs concrete
benefits.body: Give each unit an outcome, owner, input revision, output and completion evidence.

benefits.title: Catch problems before execution
benefits.body: Review hidden dependencies, missing inputs, invented thresholds and work beyond the granted scope.

walkthrough.title: Decompose the request
walkthrough.detail: Use five questions: why, who, what, how and when; label the basis for each answer.

walkthrough.title: Connect the work
walkthrough.detail: Declare prerequisites and the artifacts that cross them. Parallelize only genuinely independent work.

walkthrough.title: Review the plan
walkthrough.detail: Return ready, revise or blocked with the smallest correction and next authorized action.

use_when: A request mixes goals, tools, roles and deadlines.
Several people or agents need to work from the same plan.
An executable-looking workflow needs a scope and dependency review.
not_for: Automatic deployment authority or invented success metrics.
Executing the optional compiler's legacy YAML drafts.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use Intent to Plan on this request: improve our fictional onboarding flow and prepare a release. Separate explicit requirements from assumptions, identify missing baseline evidence, order design before implementation and make the release authority visible. Produce a plan only.
marketing.output_preview:
Fictional plan: onboarding improvement
Why: remove a reported task breakdown
Evidence: baseline and affected steps unresolved
Order: inspect → decide → implement → verify
Handoff: accepted design and task checks cross to builder
Release: separate authorized action
Verdict: revise until the missing input is resolved
marketing.proof_summary: The local native compile-tool candidate produces inspection-only drafts and preserves the existing planning and noncompile contracts. The compiler remains unchanged with its exposed 2/4 limitation. Host parser/runtime acceptance, full pytest rerun and usefulness outcomes remain unresolved.
marketing.next_step: Paste the original request and name the decisions that are already settled.
marketing.example_note: Fictional worked example. It illustrates the intended output; it is not a measured result or a real customer story.
install_notes: Requires Git and Python 3.11+ for the repository installer. The portable method itself can be read by a compatible agent without a service or provider account.
The destination is a skills-parent folder. Use the discovery path supported by your agent; ~/.agents/skills is an example, not a universal host setting.
Keep the complete installed folder, references and license together. Identical reinstall is safe; conflicts are refused. A deliberate --replace keeps a dated backup.

dataflow.installation: Shared canonical portable installer only (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/): read portable source tracked at the explicit Git pin and copy locally with SHA-256 receipts; no source text is transmitted. Legacy repository helpers copy current working-tree files and do not uniformly enforce Git pins, tracked membership or hash receipts. Native package builds and downloads have separate network, execution and storage flows described in their installation documentation.
dataflow.method: Caller supplies authorized context; existing promise and boundaries govern output.
dataflow.native_runtime: Provider/network/storage flows are owned by native interfaces and host authorization; these files do not enable them.

source_policy.revision: The shared canonical portable installer (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/) requires an explicit full 40-character Git commit and never infers latest. This guarantee does not apply uniformly to legacy or native installers; the legacy repository helper is an operator-controlled working-tree copy without Git-pin, tracked-membership or SHA-256 receipt enforcement.
source_policy.repository_rename: Public identity may change; skill folder, imports, entrypoints, tool IDs and schemas remain stable.
source_policy.research: .research/market remains local and ignored; AGENTS governs refresh.

film.heading: Ship it when ready.
film.blurb: In 73 seconds, Purl the cat pounces on a one-line request, invents a target nobody measured and hears ship it as a yes. Intent to Plan pulls the request into five threads (why, who, what, how, when), marks each said, inferred or open, weaves the work into order and gives a verdict: revise, because the baseline is missing and the release has no owner. Captions are on the player; a transcript is below.
film.note: The request, the app and the plan are a fictional example. The optional compiler shown is a prototype; the film shows how the skill behaves and reports no results.
